For those who are curious, this is how elections look like in Poland:

  • First, we vote on Sunday and Sunday only. No other days, no early voting.

  • Second, we have electoral silence. On Friday midnight all the political discussions on TV, radio, internet sites and other means cease completely. Nobody is allowed to speak publicly about any of the candidates. You can not even were shirts or caps and any other stuff with political features. You are not allowed to stick posters anymore anywhere and You can't take any of them down. If someone hears You talking politics in a shop, they can call the cops (Unless You're talking about general politics not influencing anybody's voting choice). Publishing any kinds of polls is a crime punishable with very high financial penalties. Some of the biggest website services switch off the ability to post comments under their articles so nobody can talk about politics. This is a kind of freedom of speech infringement but we all agree it serves higher purpose and we have no problem with that. It gives us whole Saturday and Sunday without any political noise so we have time to think for ourselves and reconsider whom we want to vote for. It also protects politicians from "last-minute breaking news accusations" that could be designed to bring them down unfairly.

  • Third, at the polling station we get the sheets with all the candidates from all the involved parties so we don't need to register weeks in advance whether we are this party or that party or another one. We have always more options than just two like republicans and democrats in Your case. Anybody can create a party if they want to, generally 5 or 6 get into the parliament and then the coalitions form.

We use it for buying alcohol or cigarettes, in public or private institutions and even as a passport replacement in the EU countries. It is the most important document we hold throughout the lifetime.

  • Fifth, voting is always conducted using paper sheets, we don't use electronic systems anywhere yet, since they are vulnerable to hackers and technical issues.
